Subject: Questions about backup deletion and legal hold for PHI

Hi Rachel,

Quick question from our security and legal teams about how Redwood handles deletion requests for customer data that may be in backups or DR snapshots. If MediCore issues a data-deletion request (for a patient record or dataset) or places a legal hold, how and when does that deletion propagate to: 1) live storage, 2) short-term rolling snapshots, and 3) long-term disaster recovery backups (cold storage)?

Specific asks:
- Is there an RTO/RPO dependency that could cause deleted data to remain accessible?
- Does a legal hold prevent pruning from backups? If so, how is that enforced operationally?
- If we ask for deletion, can you provide an expected timeline and any actions we need to take (support ticket, DSR form, POA)?

Appreciate a short, clear description we can share with Legal.

Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear questions. High-level answers up front, then I will follow up with an internal confirm and a short timeline: 

- Live storage: deletion (DSR) is applied immediately to the primary data plane and we mark the object as deleted in the index.
- Rolling snapshots: we retain recent rolling snapshots for disaster recovery; deleted objects are marked and become non-recoverable from hot caches within 24 hours but snapshots may still reference them until the next snapshot pruning cycle.
- Long-term DR/cold backups: these are kept for our configured backup window. Deletion does not remove objects from immutable cold backups until the retention window expires, unless a legal hold is applied.

Legal hold: when Legal requests a hold, we suspend automatic pruning for the specified identifiers and backups. That prevents automated deletion during the hold period; removal requires explicit Legal approval and a documented release.

I'll confirm exact retention windows for your account (they can vary by contract) and attach our backup flow diagram. Following up with details shortly.

Best,

Rachel — quick answers (short bullets for Legal):

- Account retention (MediCore default): rolling snapshots retained for 14 days; point-in-time backups (cold archive) retained for 365 days unless contract overrides.
- Deletion flow: DSR request -> immediate tombstone on primary (0-1 hour) -> tombstone propagated to rolling snapshots at next snapshot consolidation (up to 24 hours) -> pruning of rolling snapshots occurs during nightly sweep; object becomes unrecoverable from rolling snapshots after sweep (~24-36 hours).
- Cold backups / DR: immutable cold backups are written to long-term storage and are not auto-pruned before the configured retention. If data falls under a legal hold, we set a hold flag in the backup metadata and skip pruning for that object across all storage tiers until Legal releases the hold.
- Restore caveat: restoring from an older backup can reintroduce deleted data. If Legal requires permanent deletion, we coordinate a special workflow: create a sanitized restore, or perform a targeted purge in active store and mark related backups for manual review/removal (requires support ticket and Legal authorization).

I'll attach the authoritative policy PDF for Legal review.

Hi Jordan — following up with the consolidated, shareable description you can give to Legal and Security. We copied the relevant team members. TL;DR and then steps: 

TL;DR
- Primary deletion: immediate (tombstone applied, inaccessible) — within an hour.
- Rolling snapshots: references removed during next consolidation and the nightly pruning sweep; expect objects to be unrecoverable from rolling snapshots within 24-36 hours.
- Cold/DR backups: retained per contract (default 365 days). Deletion will not remove objects from immutable cold backups until retention expires, unless Legal places a hold or requests a targeted purge.

Legal hold behavior
- Legal hold prevents automated pruning across all tiers. We add a hold flag to backup metadata and skip the object during scheduled sweeps. Release of the hold requires documented sign-off from your Legal team and a support ticket so we can perform the next steps.

Special purge workflow (what to request if Legal needs permanent removal now)
1) Open a support ticket referencing SUP-7812 and provide the identifiers (object IDs, dates).
2) Legal supplies a release statement or confirms they do NOT want a hold.
3) We schedule a manual purge run that targets active store and marks backups for manual remove/re-encode. Note: manual purge may require re-creating some backups or sacrificial retention windows and has an operational lead time (typically 5-10 business days for complex datasets).

Notes / caveats
- Restores from backups made before deletion can reintroduce data; we recommend a sanitized restore process for any restore operation after deletions.
- RTO/RPO: no RTO/RPO will cause deleted data to be visible in the active store after tombstone — however, snapshot/backup references could be present until pruning/retention windows elapse.

Attachments and links
- redwood_backup_policy_v3.pdf (authoritative policy)
- backup_deletion_flow_diagram.png (visual flow)
- Support ticket placeholder: JIRA/SUP-7812 (we will open the ticket if you want us to kick off a manual purge)

Recommended next steps for MediCore Legal
- If you need immediate hold: reply to this thread and confirm identifiers; we will set a hold and acknowledge the objects withheld from pruning.
- If you want immediate permanent removal: provide legal authorization and we will open SUP-7812 and share an ETA for manual purge.

Happy to hop on a 20-min call if Legal wants to walk through the workflow.

Best regards,
